loc.99.1: You were not lucky: a hyper-rock concert was taking place simultaneously with your conference, and the bulk of the student was there. But anyway the conversation with those who came, was amiable and pleasant.
loc.99.2:
It turned out that you were rather popular among the students, the best part of whom were the <clr>Humans, Faes<clrEnd> and <clr>Gaals<clrEnd>. The crowd that came to your event was so large that the president had to summon an additional special force unit of the Maloqs to control it. 

The conference was rather successful - you promised to increase government-provided scholarships and educational allowances, as well as to build new hostels and structures. All in all, you were very generous in making promises and everyone liked it, except the <clr>Maloq<clrEnd> special force unit, for they knew that a real warrior will not be honeying up some yardbirds!
loc.99.3: It looked like you were a cult figure among <clr>Peleng<clrEnd> youth, and they were the main crowd who agreed to meet you. Your popularity among the other races was much lower. There were a lot of representatives of a radical student group of the Pelengs known as the "Freedom in Everything!". The group is fighting for the free trade in liquor and drugs in the university cafeteria. You had to promise them that you will solve those problems when you become President of the Planet. <ToPlanet>. The Pelengs like you even more than before for that, but the other races are hardly going to like your position.
loc.99.4: Your meeting did not provoke any boom, but it was not ignored anyway. The hall was full of members of different races and in your responses to student's questions you tried to make yourself agreeable to all the parties. They caught you off-guard and contradicting yourself a couple of times, but you joked it off very smartly, and that was very much to the tastes of the <clr>Humans<clrEnd> and <clr> Pelengs<clrEnd>. In general, your meeting could be regarded as success.
loc.99.5: Your low popularity among the Gaals, who comprised the bulk of the university higher officers played you a bad trick. At the very beginning they deliberately could not find a meeting hall for you for a long time, and during the meeting the lights were flickering out three times. Enraged, you promised that when you will be elected you will put all the incompetent leadership of the university behind the bars! This announcement put off the <clr>Faes and Gaals <clrEnd>, chirped up the <clr>Humans and Pelengs<clrEnd>, and the slow number of the <clr>Maloq<clrEnd> students were besides themselves with happiness. They secretly despised their professors, who cannot even dismantle a simple blaster...
loc.99.6: To your surprise your meeting was attended by a lot of Maloqs - it seems that you are very popular among them. This realisation played its part in your meeting address - you were mainly telling the students about the Dominators and your feasts in the struggle with them. In general, the <clr>Humans, Faes<clrEnd> and <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> liked your speech, but the <clr>Pelengs <clrEnd> and <clr>Gaals<clrEnd> were unreservedly gaping from boredom.
loc.100.0: You became a professional ranger when you were visiting a military plant. You criticised the spaceship cannons produced by the plant as if you were an expert. "This is suicide to wage the war against the Dominators with weapons like these!!!" - you harped on an on convincingly. The plant's command which was comprised of the <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> was listening to you with signs of disaffection, but all the <clr>Faeyan<clrEnd> engineers were pleased, - the engineers had been raising the issue of modernising the production for a long time before that. And the simple workers, - mainly <clr>Humans<clrEnd> and <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd> - liked the way you put down their bosses.
loc.100.1: You were courteous to the max during your tour of the plant - you praised their production procedures and the standard of the equipment, having thus pleased the <clr>Maloq<clrEnd> higher officers. Your underscored the pleasant psychological climate of the plant. Hearing your words, a <clr>Gaal<clrEnd> - plant's psychologist - turned green from pride and satisfaction! But the <clr>Humans, Pelengs<clrEnd> and <clr>Faes<clrEnd> that had to work on the plant's outdated equipment, did not think much of you...
loc.100.2: During your visit to the plant you solemnly promised to make more military awards and appropriate substantial funds for the development of new military technologies when you become president. The <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> and <clr>Faes <clrEnd> liked your statement very much, but the <clr>Gaals<clrEnd> expressed their concern about your militaristic approach. The <clr>Humans<clrEnd> and <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd> were undecided.
loc.100.3:
The visit to the plant was sabotaged - hostile <clr>Maloq<clrEnd> board of directors ordered not to let you in! 

"Stupid soldiery!" - you were shouting in front of the plant's gates. What else could you do?
loc.101.0: You seem to be honoured by the military - they organised a military parade and a muster of combat vehicles. You expressed your delight regarding the garrison's training and promised that, in the event they elect you their president, the military needs will be prioritised. This pleased the <clr>Maloq<clrEnd> generals, but the <clr>Gaals<clrEnd> and <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd> were not impressed by such a perspective.
loc.101.1: Luck was not on your sight - all the military personnel was engaged in a drill during your visit. Enraged, you blew off steam at the face of a Maloq general: his vehicles are outdated, his buildings needed to be overhauled long ago, and he is himself old enough to retire. You made it clear that if you win the election, you will award a government contract to the <clr>Faes<clrEnd> for the development of new materiel, subcontract a <clr>Peleng<clrEnd> firm to renovate the buildings and put a <clr>Human<clrEnd> general in charge of the garrison. Judging by the infuriated countenance of the garrison commander his <clr>Maloq<clrEnd> soldiers will not vote for you, but other races found your promises to their liking.
loc.101.2: The visit of the garrison was going rather routinely: you were let through all the rooms, showed the garrison's banner and the Regulations Study Room, after which you had lunch in the garrison's cafeteria. You reservedly thanked the commander for his good job. In general it was unlikely that your visit could have seriously influenced the balance of votes, it was just that the <clr>Maloqs <clrEnd> started to appreciate you better.
loc.101.3: There was a picket line in front of the entry control point comprised of the <clr>Human and Other Mammal Rights Backers and Quarter-backers Committee<clrEnd>. Their main demand was that the number of <clr>Humans<clrEnd> among the garrison officers be increased. You solemnly promised them to do exactly what they asked as soon as you become president elect, and were given a standing ovation. But in this you strongly offended the <clr>Maloq<clrEnd> senior officers, who were of a very low opinion of the combat abilities of all non-Maloqs. And no matter how honestly you praised the combat and political training of the local garrison after that, the hearts of those bluebottle-brained warriors remained unaffected.
loc.102.0: Speaking at an antiwar rally, you solemnly promised that in case you win the elections the defence spending will be cut sharply, and the funds saved will be directed for the development of sciences, art and business. You speech was OK with everyone except the <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd>.
loc.102.1: Speaking at an antiwar rally, you stated that the planet <ToPlanet> does not need its own space fleet. Although the <ToPlanet> planet never maintained its own space fleet, your words were taken negatively by the <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd>, who were dreaming of being killed in action whilst waging war against the Dominators. The <clr>Faes<clrEnd> would have received substantial subsidies for the development of new military technologies if the decision to build the fleet would be made. However the <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd>, whose illegal trade operations would have been definitely disrupted by the new fleet, will surely support you now. Your overall specific approach found popularity among the <clr>Humans<clrEnd> and <clr>Gaals<clrEnd>.
loc.102.2: You arrived when the rally had already started and missed the addresses of the first speakers. Therefore, when you promised to cut the army by the third it was taken as an outright militaristic propaganda, for the previous speakers were proposing to dismiss the army altogether! Seeing that you begin to be hissed at, you changed your approach and promised to appropriate more funds for the modernisation of the army and development of new military technologies. This completely outraged the <clr>Gaalian<clrEnd>pacifists, but brought you the votes of the <clr>Faes<clrEnd>.
loc.102.3: You were stupid enough to arrive at an antiwar rally clothed in ranger's clothes. Where your image makers were looking after all?! As a result of this the crowd, goaded by <clr>Gaalian<clrEnd> pacifists that were despising you started to hiss and yell at you. You never managed to produce a coherent speech! The pacifists are worse than pirates, and need to be jailed, all of them, - you told the reporters after the rally. Unfortunately only the <clr>Pelengs <clrEnd> and <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> could endorse a statement like that.
loc.103.0: You visited a hatch-ball match. The action did not interest you but you fearlessly spent all the 6 rounds at the stands. The <clr>Humans<clrEnd> and <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd> could not fail to notice your respect towards their game, but the other races said that spending one's time like this was ignominious.
loc.103.1: During a hatch-ball match between the Humans and the Pelengs you suddenly remembered that your rival Abu Linkoln Husseyn is a Human. So you started to actively support the Peleng team, and thus put off the <clr>Humans<clrEnd> and won over the <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd>.
loc.103.2: Today the stadium saw a principle battle between the Human and the Peleng teams. It so happened that the first of them was wearing the colours of your home planet! You were plunged in nostalgia and started to lively support the <clr>Humans<clrEnd>. Well, now you have to hope that they will repay you when they will be casting their ballots, but your prestige among the <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd> lowered considerably after this match.
loc.104.0: You were somewhat surprised that the bulk of the jail inmates was comprised of the <clr>Humans<clrEnd> and <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd>. Your promise to announce a presidential clemency if you will be elected was widely supported among the mentioned races. But all the other races were only put on the alert by such a prospect.
loc.104.1:
Unfortunately the prison governor, a Maloq, refused to let you in! Well, public poll analysts were rightly urging you to improve your positions among this race...

You were quick to strike back. At an improvised rally in front of the prison gates you solemnly promised to crack down on the corruption in the penitentiary system as soon as you get elected. This statement was received hostile among the <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> and <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd>, but the other races were pleased.
loc.104.2: Someone from the first cells threw a lump of stingy swamp mud at you - that's what means a low popularity among the Pelengs! You decided to see no more cells after this incident, but speak to the guard and administration instead. You voiced an opinion that the imprisonment regime must be stiffened and started to give out lavish promises. The guards (mainly <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> and <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd>) - will receive a greater pay, the <clr>Faeyan<clrEnd> engineers will receive funds for the modernisation of locks and alarm. Only the <clr>Peleng<clrEnd> prisoners and <clr>Gaalian<clrEnd> right activists found nothing pleasant in your promises.
loc.104.3: Today you visited that part of the prison where the state prisoners were confined - mainly <clr>Humans<clrEnd> and <clr>Gaals<clrEnd>. You promised to liberalise the laws and improve imprisonment conditions. This was applauded by everyone, except the <clr>Maloq<clrEnd> guards, who were listening to you with open disgust.
loc.105.0: You spent some time wandering about the exhibition halls, expressing your delight concerning the Gaalian iike-baanas, in which you did not understand a thing. This was acclaimed by the <clr>Gaals<clrEnd>. The <clr>Humans<clrEnd> - exhibition sponsors - were very glad with free publicity. But the <clr>Maloq<clrEnd> guards were fully despising you, - well, those tough guys just cannot comprehend abstract art - what can be done?!
loc.105.1: Walking around the exhibition halls, you were so vividly expressing your admiration towards the iike-baanas, that you subconsciously touched one and broke it down. This somehow poisoned the effect of your speech, although the <clr>Gaals<clrEnd> were not vindictive and were apt to forgive. But the <clr>Humans<clrEnd> - the exhibition sponsors - were very disappointed, because now they had to pay substantial compensation to the author of the broken piece. And the <clr>Maloq<clrEnd> guards were smiling as wide as their stupid faces allowed - you were the cause of their entertainment during on-duty hours that would be a dreadful boredom otherwise!
loc.105.2: During the tour around the hall you became so lyrical that promised to make the art of making iike-baanas a mandatory part of school program in case you are elected. <clr>Gaals<clrEnd> and <clr>Humans<clrEnd> were filled with admiration because of this, but the <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> were enraged, and the <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd> with the <clr>Faes<clrEnd> were not so happy with the idea to burden their children with a nonsense like that.
loc.106.0:
You decided to relax and visited a local fairy-tale amusement park. You were getting fun as a child the whole night: riding on the merry-go-round, wandering in the wonderland, swimming in the magic pool, you even took part in an auction, purchasing a firedrake's tooth and an old witch's broom for your collection of trifles... 

The newspapers this day published detailed reports about your entertainment acts. In general, the <clr>Humans, Pelengs<clrEnd> and <clr>Gaals<clrEnd> evaluated your ability to have fun as positive, but the <clr>Faes<clrEnd> and <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> were enraged by such a valueless and unproductive time spending.
loc.106.1:
You decided to relax and visited a local fairy-tale amusement park. But soon you got sick and tired of just walking around the tree-lined paths and of riding on the merry-go-rounds. Suddenly you conceived of an idea how to improve your rating among the <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd>! 

Within five minutes you were standing with a sword in hand aiming it at a triple-headed firedrake in a kind of gladiator fight. You were able to duck from its fire-throwing heads at first, and even manages to hack down one of them. But after this, the firedrake craftily hit you with its tail and you fell on the ground. Fairy-tale monster could have crushed you with its carcass, but your bodyguard was quick enough to shoot it down from a blaster.

The press was commenting on your actions for quite a time after the event. The <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd> - the owners of the park - were enraged by the spoilage of big dollar property and demanded to reimburse the damage. The <clr>Faes <clrEnd> and <clr>Gaals<clrEnd> were also disapproving of your purposeless risk. But you accomplished your task - the <clr>Humans<clrEnd> and, especially, the <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> liked your audacious and reckless vagary to the bottom of their hearts!
loc.106.2: Walking around the fairy-tale amusement park, you decided to mix business with pleasure and improve your rating among the <clr>Faes<clrEnd> and <clr>Gaals<clrEnd>. In order to do so you visited the wise-persons amusement section and spent the whole night answering the Riddles of the Sphynx and Calistrate Wiseast. You failed to gain the main prize, but the elector's value and not the victory, but the participation! Right, the <clr>Faes <clrEnd> and <clr>Gaals<clrEnd> were impressed by your quest for knowledge, although <clr>Humans, Pelengs<clrEnd> and <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> seemed to be preferring other kinds of entertainment.
loc.107.0: The officers spent the whole night introducing you to the xenopark. Looking at the animals of all types you were vividly expressing your admiration. In doing so you took a veterbratosaur for an anemonobrate, and a ducklapus for a quackadile, which caused a good deal of laugh on the part of the <clr>Faeyan<clrEnd> students who happened to be in the park making some naturalistic work there. But a good round sum from planet <FromPlanet>'s funds, that you donated for the development of the xenopark, will surely bring you a lot of <clr>Peleng<clrEnd> votes.
loc.107.1: An unpleasant incident occurred in front of the xenopark - picketers from Animal Rights Organisation (mainly - <clr>Gaals<clrEnd> and <clr>Humans<clrEnd>) pelted you with rotten tomatoes! In return you made a statement in the press that when you become president you will develop the network of the xenoparks further and will allow the scientists to experiment on animals. After such a statement you can count that the votes of the <clr>Pelengs <clrEnd> and <clr>Faes<clrEnd> are yours.
loc.107.2: You were not so popular among the <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd>, owners of the xenopark, therefore they did not provide any special service during your visit to the park. This had its imprint on your mood, and after the walk around the park you told the reporters that you find the conditions in which the animals are kept to be very poor. The <clr>Gaals<clrEnd> and <clr>Humans<clrEnd> - renowned animal rights activists - liked statement, but any of the other races definitely no. And even a round amount that you donated for the keeping of the animals, did not alleviate the green hearts of the xenopark owners.
loc.108.0:
- Cool, we have equal votes! - you exclaimed. - Does this mean that we both won?

- No! - Kill Young answered, trying to get away from you ASAP. - This means that you both lost!

And really, Abu Linkoln Husseyn's advisors were getting away from him as quick as yours from you. The guards took you both, placed together to the wall and shot from a blaster - in full compliance with democratic traditions of planet <ToPlanet>...
loc.109.0: - Well, what is there to say?, Kill Young said surprisedly. <ToPlanet> is a typical marginal little planet that tries hard to make a name for itself. To be honest, it's not officially acknowledged by other planets yet, and all their reference books list <ToPlanet> as uninhabited. At some point in history, it was the place where all the criminals of all races of the Galaxy were deported, but a long time passed since then, and people here became cultured. The local population is small comparing to other planets at only {[p2]+[p3]+[p4]+[p5]+[p6]} K. However, the races are almost all evenly represented, which is unique compared to other planets in the galaxy. The public here is politically active, <clr>no less than 90%<clrEnd> of the electorate participate in the vote. The social groups are the same as elsewhere, although each race has their own occupations which they are accustomed to... I hope that answers your question?
jump.2.text: Go to the electoral committee and see how the vote count is done
jump.24.desc: Today, the parliament of the <ToPlanet> planet has issued a decree on providing access to the polling stations for all the <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd>, that were deported to the <ToPlanet> planet from other planets for drug trafficking. The number of Peleng voters increased by [p23] thou. as a result
jump.25.desc: Today, Gaalian rights activists achieved the recovery of electoral right for the <clr>Maloq<clrEnd> dissidents and pacifists. The number of Maloq voters increased by [p23] thou.
jump.26.desc: Today, the parliament of the <ToPlanet> plant issued a decree on the lowering of the electoral age qualification limit for the <clr>Faes<clrEnd> to {[22..28]} years. The number of Faeyan voters increased by [p23] thou.
jump.27.desc: Today Faeyan Ethics Committee of the <ToPlanet>'s parliament insisted that the <clr>Faes<clrEnd>, who tasted alcohol or drugs be deprived of the right to vote. Thus a total of [p23] thou. Faes will not be allowed to vote.
jump.28.desc: Today the Human and other Mammal Rights Backers and Quarter-backers Committee succeeded in providing the right to vote for all the imprisoned <clr>Humans<clrEnd>, thus increasing the number of Human voters by [p23] thou.
jump.41.desc: Today the government of the <ToPlanet> planet provided Green Card for all the <clr>Gaalian<clrEnd> fugitives, that arrived to the planet during the past year. Now extra [p23] thou. Gaals will be able to come to the polling stations.
jump.42.desc: Today, the radical wing of the Maloq faction of the <ToPlanet> planet enacted a law that prohibits voting for any of the <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd>, who served less than {[3..7]} years in the army. The number of Maloq voters sharply decreased by [p23] thou.
jump.43.desc: Today the Peleng drug dealers lobby in the <ToPlanet>'s parliament demanded that the <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd> who spent no time in prison, be deprived of the right to vote. After short debates, the demand was satisfied, and the number of Peleng votes reduced by [p23] thou.
jump.44.desc: According to the decision of the Children Protection Committee of the <ToPlanet> parliament, the <clr>Humans<clrEnd> will be allowed to vote only when they turn {[14..16]}, and not {[9..11]}, as it used to be. This decreased the number of Human voters by [p23] thou.
jump.45.desc: Today the Peleng, Human and Maloq factions of the <ToPlanet>'s parliament insisted that the <clr>Gaals<clrEnd> who are older than {10*[15..20]} years be deprived of the right to vote, providing such reasons that the members of their own races do not live that long. The number of Gaalian voters thus reduced by [p23] thou.
jump.46.text: Strange that such a warm post is claimed by only two candidates. What's wrong?
jump.47.text: What?! If I lose, I will be killed? I'm getting out of here immediately!!!
jump.48.text: OK! Good bye, folks, I need to have some sleep!
jump.49.text: Ok, guys, see you all tomorrow, it's time for me to sleep!
jump.51.text: Scram before it's not to late!!!
jump.52.text: Ok, I'll sign it, as we agreed!
jump.53.text: Ha!!! You think I am a moron?! Now I will rule planet <ToPlanet> on my own!.
jump.58.text: In time of trouble all reasonable citizens of the Galaxy must lay their lives in preventing the Dominators' threat!
jump.58.desc:
- Is he really such an idiot or just looks like it? - a baffled <clr>Peleng<clrEnd> journalist asked his <clr>Human<clrEnd> colleague.

- Well, one will go through many things to reach presidential chair... - the latter answered rather philosophically.  

Your patriotic rhetoric produced no effect. But the journalists of other races who are no so sophisticated in political intrigues liked it well enough at least.
jump.59.text: When you are flying in a bottomless blackness of the space, which is packed with the light of faraway stars, the truth can be revealed to you in the light of prominence - this is the eternity!
jump.59.desc: - I wonder, where does he get such dope? - a <clr>Peleng<clrEnd> journalist murmured in admiration. Others were in a state of complete trans after your response.
jump.61.desc: Today at the meeting with the local drag trafficking tycoons Abu Linkoln Husseyn promised that in case he is elected president he will legalise drugs for sale in schools. This scandalous statement shocked the voters of all races but the <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd>, who proclaimed Abu Linkoln Husseyn to be a hero of the Peleng race.
jump.63.desc: Today Abu Linkoln Husseyn told his press conference that he considers the <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> to be an inferior race. This statement undermined his positions among Maloq voters, but all the other races seemed to like it.
jump.64.text: Profession of a ranger means freedom and the possibility to find one's own self!
jump.64.desc:
- Dog's crap! - a <clr>Maloq<clrEnd> journalist exploded in anger. - If you want freedom - enlist in the army!

- Or engage in science, - a <clr>Faeyan<clrEnd> unexpectedly backed the Maloq. 

The others left you response without comment, but seemed to be overall pleased with your position.
jump.65.text: So what? No thirst work - go, loot the transports, and track in dope. The main thing is to get away from the Dominators in time!
jump.65.desc: Your insolent and cynical response enraged all but the <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd>. You had to wait 30 minutes when the guard was calming down the journalists and tried to get them all sit back to their places.
jump.66.text: Well who can understand him? One has to do something...
jump.66.desc: Your flat response made no impression on those present.
jump.69.text: Gaal, so that you would not even think of asking such idiotic questions!
jump.69.desc: Enraged to the bottom of his heart, the <clr>Gaalian<clrEnd> professor took his seat. But your response provoked unanimous applause of all the rest present in the hall, with most violent ovation heard from the <clr>Maloq<clrEnd> and <clr>Peleng<clrEnd> seats.
jump.70.text: Faeyan, because it is easy to handle him!
jump.70.desc: By all appearance, your pragmatic approach found support only among the <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd>. The <clr>Humans<clrEnd> remained indifferent, <clr>Gaals<clrEnd> were hoping for another answer, and the <clr>Faes <clrEnd> were outraged to the marrow of their bones. And even stupid <clr>Maloq<clrEnd> countenances bore the sight of contempt to such a cowardly tactics.
jump.71.text: Human, for their meat is most tender!
jump.71.desc: - Have you tasted it already?! - a <clr>Human<clrEnd> journalist next to you shouted throwing the lens of a stereocamera at you. His argument seemed very convincing for the <clr>Gaals and Faes<clrEnd>, who were renowned for their special respect for logical arguments. And only the <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd> were smiling rapaciously, meanwhile the  <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> were turning their stupid noddles around trying to understand why there's such a turmoil in the conference hall.
jump.72.text: Peleng, for they are capable of any kind of beastliness!
jump.72.desc:
- Wrong!!! - the <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd> who were present in the hall exclaimed. - We are not capable of any beastliness, we would generously help you in eating someone else!

<clr>Gaals<clrEnd> also did not endorse your response, but the members of the other races seemed to share the opinion of the Pelengs.
jump.73.text: Maloq, for their meat will last long!
jump.73.desc: The <clr>Faes, Humans and Pelengs<clrEnd> liked the sharp logic of you answer. One <clr>Gaal<clrEnd> was shaking his head in sadness - he definitely saw some moral and ethic misconceptions in it. But you could not occupy yourself with him, because a group of <clr>Maloq<clrEnd> journalists somehow had decided to smash your face together. Your panic retreat under the table, where you were sitting waiting for the storm to calm down while the security was trying to restore order, would not add to your reputation among this militaristic race.
jump.74.text: Dominator, as they are our common enemy!
jump.74.desc:
- But this is stupid! - one of the <clr>Faes<clrEnd> said. - Dominators posses quite a different metabolism, which cannot be complied with any of the other races of  the Galaxy! You cannot eat a Dominator!!!

But all the rest including the <clr>Gaals<clrEnd>, seemed to like the way you got around the catch so that the professor shut up. And the <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> produced a short ovation as a reaction on the "enemy" word.
jump.75.text: No one, because the eating of reasonable beings is absolutely non-ethical!
jump.75.desc:
The <clr>Gaal<clrEnd> applauded - he seemed to be waiting for just this kind of answer. But a <clr>Peleng<clrEnd> said:

- Stupid! In this case the others will eat you! Or, are you proposing that all die of hunger?

After a spontaneously risen discussion most of the <clr>Humans<clrEnd> took up the Gaalian standpoint, and the <clr>Faes<clrEnd> agreed with the logic of the Pelengs. Its just that stupid <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> did not understand a thing again.
jump.78.desc:
You ordered to organise a press conference and got down to the preparation of the text for your address. But within 30 minutes a disheartened Kill Young called you saying that the journalists were sick and tired of your speeches already, and the event would not take place. Enraged, you crumpled up the paper with your speech and threw it in the trash can. You spent so much labour, used so many tricks of stylistics and applied so many refined insults on your competitor - and all in vain!!!

You decided to proclaim a short-term strike as a protest and do nothing more before lunch. Hoo-pa!
jump.79.desc: Today Abu Linkoln Husseyn promised at an antiwar rally to ban free weapons trade on the planet <ToPlanet> if he is elected president. The <clr>Faes<clrEnd> and <clr>Gaals<clrEnd> took this promise with open heart, unlike the <clr>Humans<clrEnd> and the <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd>, who were making big bucks on weapons trading. Moreover, the <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> considered this statement to be a personal insult directed at their race.
jump.80.desc: Today Abu Linkoln Husseyn announced at his press conference that he considered all scientists and especially humanities research fellows to be useless mouths. All <clr>Faeyan<clrEnd> and <clr>Gaalian <clrEnd> journalists, as well as part of the <clr>Humans<clrEnd> left the conference room as a protest. Although the <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd> and the <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> left in the room spent quite a time throwing their new idol up in the air.
jump.81.desc: Today Abu Linkoln Husseyn donated a large amount of money for the opening of a column dedicated to all planet <ToPlanet>'s citizens, who died in action against the Dominators. This decision proved to be popular among all the planet's population, especially among the <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd>.
jump.86.text: The taxes will stay on the same level they are now
jump.87.text: Familiarise yourself with the data and get to bed
jump.88.text: I would like to finish my press conference on that: now, it's lunchtime!
jump.89.text: I would like to finish my press conference on that: now, it's lunchtime!
jump.90.text: I would like to finish my press conference on that: now, it's lunchtime!
jump.91.desc: Today Abu Linkoln Husseyn said in the interview to the <clr>"Young Generation"<clrEnd> Magazine that he could not tolerate hatch-ball. This at once cut him short of much of the <clr>Peleng and Human<clrEnd> sympathies, although the polls show that the <clr> Maloqs, Faes and Humans<clrEnd> share this position completely.
jump.94.text: The colour of blood of enemies killed by me
jump.94.desc: <clr>Gaals and Faes<clrEnd> were apparently jarred by open violence inherent to your answer. Although the members of other races liked its honesty and openness, the tender nature of the <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> was impressed most of all.
jump.95.text: Its not the colour that's important, it's composition of the colours
jump.95.desc: The <clr>Gaal<clrEnd> started nodding satisfactorily - he was apparently inclined to hear something like that. Although someone of the <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> fetched up on hearing the word "composition". Other reporters present in the hall were not impressed by your statement at all.
jump.96.desc: Red faces of the <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> were distorted out of contempt for such an answer, the <clr>Gaals<clrEnd> must have known more beautiful colours, but the <clr>Pelengs, Humans and Faes<clrEnd> shared your views concerning the beauty of a colour grade completely.
jump.97.desc: Laughter in the Human seats showed that this response brought you uncontested sympathies of the <clr>Humans<clrEnd>. The <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd> also stayed pleased with it. But members of other races treated boozing with much less tolerance, therefore their faces were somehow distorted on hearing this.
jump.98.desc: Today Abu Linkoln Husseyn promised at a rally in front of a military plant to increase spending on defence already in the first quarter of his presidency. <clr>Humans and Maloqs<clrEnd>, working at that plant, made him an ovation, but the circles of <clr>Gaalian<clrEnd> rights activists and <clr>Faeyan<clrEnd> pacifists expressed a great concern about the society's military tendency.
jump.99.desc: Presidential candidate Abu Linkoln Husseyn issued a decree on general pardon for all the planet <ToPlanet>'s prisoners. The decree will be enforced as soon as Abu Linkoln Husseyn is elected president. Now the <clr>Pelengs <clrEnd> are eagerly waiting for him to be elected. <clr>Gaals<clrEnd> claimed they also endorse this decision fully, for many renowned Gaalian rights activist think that confinement contradicts the right of all the sapiens for free migration. The circle of the <clr>Maloqs, Humans<clrEnd> and especially <clr>Faes <clrEnd> expressed their concern that this move can provoke a sharp boom of criminality, unrest, anarchy and other instability of the society.
jump.101.text: I would like to finish my press conference on that - sorry, it's lunchtime!
jump.103.text: Well, why can't you kill the chief, and that's that!
jump.103.desc: You reply was very well taken by the <clr>Maloqs, Pelengs and Humans<clrEnd>, but the <clr>Faes and Gaals<clrEnd> were apparently more accustomed with solving financial problems in a more civilised way.
jump.104.text: I consider computer gaming as complete idiocracy and time spent in vain!
jump.104.desc: The reaction of the crowd showed that the <clr>Maloqs, Pelengs and Faes <clrEnd> also thought that time can be spent more useful than that. ("Science!", "Drill!", "Pirating!" - these were the shouts heard from their seats.). But the outraged <clr>Humans<clrEnd> were yelling insults at you quite a time after that, and the <clr>Gaals<clrEnd> were put off by the harshness and flatness of your reply.
jump.105.desc: Presidential candidate Abu Linkoln Husseyn proclaimed that on the first day of his presidency he will introduce the Prohibition. This was very much liked by the <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> and <clr>Faes<clrEnd>, but the <clr>Humans <clrEnd> and <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd> now will not so eagerly vote for Husseyn.
jump.107.desc: Today a blast sounded in the Faeyan research and development institute as a result of careless treatment of hexanotoluol. The death toll amounted to over [p23] thousand <clr>Faes<clrEnd>! Abu Linkoln Husseyn already donated 10.000 cr to the victims' relatives fund, through which he earned a respect of the Faeyan race.
jump.109.desc: The training of the <clr>Maloq<clrEnd> corps of the planet <ToPlanet>'s armed forces ended in tragedy today. One of the pseudonuclear warhead missile wandered from its course and landed in the location of the 8th infantry regiment, set up for a parade. The blast carried the lives of [p23] thousand Maloqs. Abu Linkoln Husseyn accused the <clr>Faeyan<clrEnd> scientists in deliberate development of defective missile pointing devices for the army and promised to deal with the culprits when he will be elected president of planet <ToPlanet>. The Maloq military accepted this statement with enthusiasm, but the renowned Faeyan scientists suggested that the members of their race vote against Husseyn or just ignore the elections.
jump.110.desc: A terrible wreck happened in a densely populated <clr>Human<clrEnd> quarter of the capital today when a cargo astracopter crashed 10 minutes after take off! According to preliminary data, the death toll was no less than [p23] thousand people! Specialists think that the wreck of the astracopter occurred due to defected fuel, the craft was filled with at a local spaceport. Abu Linkoln Husseyn promised to audit the accounts of the <clr>Peleng<clrEnd> suppliers of the fuel when he is elected and severely punish the culprits.
jump.111.desc: Mass suicide of [p23] thousand <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd> - members of a totalitarian sect "Path to Nowhere" - shocked today all the progressive public of the planet <ToPlanet>. The suicide was caused by a narcotic vision of the spiritual leader of the sect - lyakusha Hash Khan - of a near end of the world and the ban to trade drugs. Abu Linkoln Husseyn expressed his sincere wish to outlaw any totalitarian sects on the planet <ToPlanet>. In the light of the latest events, this statement was received with enthusiasm among the masses, especially that of the Peleng.
jump.112.desc: A terrible act of terrorism in the Gaalian Fine Arts and Abstract Logic Museum claimed the lives of [p23] thousands <clr>Gaals<clrEnd>! A radical <clr>Maloq Order<clrEnd> group claimed responsibility for this terror. The group is fighting for the Maloqs to be pronounced the superior race and all the other races to be deprived of the right to vote. Abu Linkoln Husseyn stated that he will hang the Maloq terrorists on the lampposts. The Gaals, usually not so disposed to violence were excited to hear that, but the radical Maloqs proclaimed Abu Linkoln Husseyn Maloq race Public Enemy No. 1.
jump.113.text: All you need is a good trade. Buy cheap, sell with a higher price, betray partners from time to time - and everything will be okey-dokey.
jump.113.desc: <clr>Humans and Pelengs<clrEnd> unconditionally shared your opinion about how to gain success in life and computer games. The <clr>Gaals<clrEnd> were frowning on hearing about cheating the partners, and the <clr>Maloqs <clrEnd> were spitting on hearing the word "trade".
jump.114.text: The colour of dead Dominator parts
jump.114.desc: You reply made no impression in general, as the reporters sitting in the conference hall were rarely leaving Planet <ToPlanet> and could hardly imagine what this colour might be.
jump.115.text: You should buy the local booze for all your money, make the chief drunk, and you can count that the idol is yours!
jump.115.desc: <clr>Humans, Pelengs and Maloqs<clrEnd> laughed at that - yes, that's how it is best to treat other races, without mittens!!! But some mumbling against "non-ethical methods" and "Providing booze to primeval races" was heard from the <clr>Faeyan and Gaalian<clrEnd> seats.
jump.117.text: I would like to finish my press conference on that: now, it's lunchtime!
jump.118.text: This is a slander about Maloq fighters! I will not answer this question!!!
jump.118.desc: After such an answer a huge ovation from the <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> was guaranteed! But all the others did not even try to hide contempt for your stupidity, since the drawbacks of the Maloq technologies have long become a story...
jump.119.desc: Your phrase cased great laugh among the <clr>Humans and Pelengs<clrEnd> - these guys understand what a good phase is! But the <clr>Gaals and Maloqs<clrEnd> were sincerely outraged: the first did not like the dirtiness of your expression, and the second your disrespect for the command. And only the <clr>Faes<clrEnd> remained indifferent, because for the hermaphrodites it was difficult to appreciate the whole strength of your words.
jump.123.text: I think we will find individual sponsors for that
jump.124.text: Ah, yes, we will definitely cancel that tax
jump.125.text: I told you - everything will be as it used to be!!!
jump.126.text: This issue will be resolved independently
jump.128.text: This is not the most horrible thing that might happen
jump.129.text: Well, we are not going to raise taxes a lot! Well, a little bit, maybe...
jump.130.text: The main thing is that the planet have enough money to feed the presidential administration, all the rest is unessential
jump.131.text: Well, we will definitely abolish all unjust taxes and will add just ones, but in general everything will remain as it used to be!
jump.132.text: It's the first time I hear about a problem like that. What do you mean?!
jump.133.text: I think we can subsidise business from the budget, you should not be so concerned about it.
jump.134.text: If such a problem arises will we be solving it at that time. Why beat brains with it now?
jump.135.text: I think that the command does not have anything to do with it
jump.135.desc: You reply was not so logical, but the <clr>Maloqs and Gaals<clrEnd> liked it because of its patriotism and objectivity respectively. But the <clr>Pelengs, Humans and Faes<clrEnd>, judging by their grins, were not of a high opinion about your mental capability.
jump.136.text: I think that I would sue him, if I would survive such a mess
jump.136.desc: Your reasonable and civilised response was to everyone's liking, except the <clr>Pelengs and Maloqs<clrEnd> - the first apparently were not in support of legal ways of reaching a goal, and the second just could not imagine how one can sue its own commander.
jump.137.text: I think I am the one to blame - I should not have agreed to test a Maloq fighter
jump.137.desc: Your reply to the provocative question sounded rather reasonable so that everyone, naturally except the <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd>, was pleased. The Maloqs thought is was a bold attempt to blacken their fighters.
jump.138.text: You need to study the culture of that tribe, learn their folkways and customs. Why, they can just give this idol to you themselves!
jump.138.desc: The <clr>Gaals and Faes<clrEnd> liked the tactics you proposed - really, the knowledge is the best clue to anything! Only the <clr>Maloqs and Pelengs <clrEnd> were contemptuously gaping at your words, they surely knew some more effective methods! The <clr>Humans<clrEnd> were divided on that.
jump.139.text: I would try to shock this tribe by the technical progress - I would show them my spaceship, weaponry and materiel. I think the locals would become more compliant!
jump.139.desc: The <clr>Faes<clrEnd>, were impressed by this line of action the most, for they were so proud of their technical progress. The <clr>Humans, Pelengs, and Maloqs<clrEnd>, seemed to be also satisfied. Only the <clr>Gaals<clrEnd> poked some ethical problems in this...
jump.140.text: This game implies stealing the cultural values of the primeval races, it should be outlawed at once and for all!
jump.140.desc: After such a reply the <clr>Gaals<clrEnd> applauded you in standing, and the stupid <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd>, were quick to follow suit, for they would rather miss a round of kinza drinking than the opportunity to outlaw something. But the <clr>Pelengs, Faes<clrEnd> and especially <clr>Humans<clrEnd> did not see anything criminal in it.
jump.141.text: Unfortunately I am colour blind, daltonian - I cannot distinguish colours
jump.141.desc: Shooch Yaa sat down ashamed. The reaction of the hall showed that your forced confession filled the <clr>Faeyan, Gaalian and Human<clrEnd> hearts with pity and the <clr>Maloq and Peleng<clrEnd> hearts with contempt.
jump.144.text: I would like to finish my press conference on that: now, it's lunchtime!
jump.145.text: I would pay the money - it's stupid to lose the life and spaceship because of them money
jump.145.desc: This judicious decision impressed the <clr>Gaals<clrEnd> (life is more expensive than money!), <clr>Faes<clrEnd> (the ship's depreciation value would exceed the sum of the ransom) and <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd> (Yes you have to pay the pirates, se la vie!). But the proverbial greed of the <clr>Humans<clrEnd> could not tolerate parting with the money. And, as concerns the <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd>, after a short fight stopped, the adherents of fighting easily won over the small amount of combat capable unit followers.
jump.146.text: I would engage in fight! This is the highest honour for any reasonable being to die in action!
jump.146.desc:
- Excellent, <Ranger>! - Karra Bach exclaimed sitting down accompanied by excited roar of other <clr>Maloq<clrEnd> journalists. - I would not expect any other reply!

But the other races were waiting for a more practical decision from you, as their dull countenances well expressed.
jump.147.text: I would try to jump into a hyper - you can always heal yourself there, having shot a couple of pirates
jump.147.desc:
- It's more likely that the pirates will shoot you in the hyper! - someone of the <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd> shouted offended. Looks like you answer will not gain support among that race.

But all the rest were in general pleased. The <clr>Faes and Gaals<clrEnd> enjoyed the logic of your decision and the desire to destroy the pirates of the hyperstate, <clr>Humans<clrEnd> liked the fact that there was no need to pay the money, and<clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> - that the fight would take place anyway.
jump.148.text: I would begin negotiations, bargain and hang out for terms, kill time and try to get to the nearest planet
jump.148.desc: Your tactics were fully endorsed by the <clr>Humans<clrEnd> - the acknowledged masters of the Galaxy in bargaining and killing time. The <clr>Faes and Gaals<clrEnd> also approved of the idea of a diplomatic settlement of the conflict. But the <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd> were enraged with so bashful an attempt to trick a pirate (well, you think he will talk to you that much - he will shoot you an that's that!), and the <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> despised the idea of bargaining instead of fighting.
jump.149.text: I would pay him, then land at a planet, repair the ship, take off, find that pirate and victimise him!
jump.149.desc:
The reaction was ambiguous.

The <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> decided that to postpone the fight until the conditions get better is a good manoeuvre!.
- The main thing is to get double from the pirate later, - claimed the <clr>Humans<clrEnd>.
- Revenge is a base animal feeling! - the <clr>Gaals<clrEnd> insisted.
- The pirates should be destroyed with all the means possible! - proclaimed the <clr>Faes<clrEnd>.
- Pirate is not an idiot himself! He will not wait before you will be repaired! He will jump into another system and that's all! - all the <clr>Pelengs <clrEnd> shouted.

Within five minutes the noise in the hall died out.
jump.164.text: All the areas will have the same priority
jump.165.text: We will develop new military technologies
jump.166.text: We will construct new military plants
jump.167.text: We will increase the term of military duty for five years
jump.168.text: We will procure new weapons from industrially developed countries
jump.169.text: Why strengthen it? It is strong enough
jump.171.text: We will dismiss the army, and transfer military expenses for peaceful purposes. No one will attack us anyway!
jump.172.text: We will have to promulgate a more rigid penal code
jump.173.text: We will build new prisons and imprison one and all
jump.175.text: We will reconsider all the cases and free all who were convicted unjustly
jump.176.text: We will proclaim general clemency on the day I am elected
jump.177.text: We will have to conduct a reform of the criminal court system, with meticulous observance of all the formalities stipulated by the law.
jump.178.text: I would like to finish my press conference on that - sorry, it's lunchtime!
jump.183.text: I would like to finish my press conference on that - sorry, it's lunchtime!
jump.186.text: I would like to finish my press conference on that - sorry, it's lunchtime!
jump.187.text: I would like to finish my press conference on that - sorry, it's lunchtime!
jump.200.text: We will not do anything, we will leave anything as it is
jump.201.text: Everything depends on the situation, if it is profitable for me - I believe, if not - I believe not
jump.201.desc: Your response was fully endorsed by the <clr>Humans and Pelengs<clrEnd>, most of them were going along the same lines in philosophy. All the rest were disgusted by your cynicism and most of all the <clr>Gaals<clrEnd>.
jump.202.text: If I win this election - this means God exists!
jump.202.desc: Now even the Maloqs understood that this was a joke, but not all of them liked it...
jump.203.text: No, because the rangers' Charter does not say anything about God
jump.203.desc: Only the <clr>Maloqs and Faes<clrEnd> took your response at it's face value. The former liked it but the latter were disappointed in your mental capabilities. The <clr>Humans<clrEnd> received your joke positively, <clr>Gaals<clrEnd> more negatively, and the <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd> were indifferent.
jump.204.text: I do believe! I recall how having doped myself with cocaine I conversed with him for quite a time...
jump.204.desc: Your mentioning cocaine made <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd> to start a vivid ovation. <clr>Humans<clrEnd> also appreciated your humour. Although your popularity went down greatly among the <clr>Gaals, Faes and Maloqs<clrEnd> - these races treat their health too seriously.
jump.205.text: Yes, the Universe must have been created by someone, if not by God, then by whom?
jump.205.desc: Od-delani Tall Mud could not appreciate your words in spite of all their logic. He started arguing, citing quotes from his own magazine. The <clr>Faes <clrEnd>, seemed to be sharing his views, but the <clr>Gaals<clrEnd> started arguing it was all vice versa. The <clr>Humans and Pelengs <clrEnd>, acknowledged some logic in your answer, so that the offended Faes soon lost the argument. And even the <clr>Maloq<clrEnd> sector was hooting loudly, showing their negative attitude towards such a theme for discussion.
jump.206.text: No, because God's existence has not been proved scientifically
jump.206.desc: This was exactly the thing the <clr>Faes<clrEnd> expected to hear from you. In any case the triangle faces of the Faes who were present were smiling wide and turned lily, which was the sign of their good humour. But the <clr>Gaals <clrEnd> and especially the <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> were not impressed by this argument. The <clr>Humans and Pelengs<clrEnd>, were not the least interested in the question about God.
jump.207.desc: Meaningful use of unclear words with unclear meaning is the best way to achieve respect of the <clr>Gaals, Fayans<clrEnd> and, perhaps, <clr>Humans<clrEnd>. But all the <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd> do not approve of such a style, and the <clr>Malloqs<clrEnd> usually feel sick when they hear such words...
jump.208.text: Free press hampers the conduct of an effective policy, so I will not have free press during my presidency!
jump.209.text: Surely, the press will stay free! Well, maybe we will censor something this time or that...
jump.210.text: The only really free press is the one that backs the supreme power!
jump.211.text: My opinion is that the press must be eliminated and all the journalists be shot down! It's the most useless of professions!!!
jump.212.text: Freedom of speech - this is the highest value, so nothing is to be spared for the free press!
jump.213.text: The press will be absolutely free! We will publish a Drug Addict Journal and Young Terrorist Newspaper, as well as all the rest of the editions that are being unjustly suppressed by the current regime!
jump.214.text: The press? For all I care about the press, let it live, I don't read newspapers anyway...
jump.215.text: I think this is the most useless item of expenditure. We will cut it down first!
jump.216.text: The spending on sport is not enough! This should be our policy's priority!
jump.217.text: I recognise only the intellectual sports - chess, draughts, making of iike-baanas. All the rest is crap!
jump.218.text: This is all trifling! There are more important areas. And our main funds will be directed there!
jump.219.text: You can make good money on sport, if you manage to make a timely investment. We will first develop the economically rewarding sports!
jump.220.text: I am myself not interested in sports, so it's for the house members to decide how much to spend on it
jump.221.text: We will primarily subsidise mass physical training and child sport, because they are the nation's health. And big sport will manage to survive without government support...
jump.222.text: We will lay off all chair warmers and that's all!
jump.223.text: The funding for the education and science has been reduced substantially
jump.224.text: We will subsidise only the useful areas of science such as the development of new armament
jump.225.text: Our policy will be to prioritise on the development of science!
jump.226.text: Everything will stay as it used to be - I can't see a point in changing anything
jump.227.text: We will increase research fellows' and professors' salaries
jump.228.text: Conducting our own research is a waste of time. It would be cheaper to steal from the neighbours, wouldn't it?
jump.230.text: I am taking up exercise every morning!
jump.230.desc: <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> gave you an ovation, for according to the regulations, the real warrior must do fitness and shooting exercises every day. <clr>Humans<clrEnd> and <clr>Gaals<clrEnd> also acknowledged the usefulness if regular physical training to some extent. And only the lazy <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd>, and the <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> who despised all physical exercise were not the least impressed by your response..
jump.231.text: I don't have time to go to the gym
jump.231.desc: Your confession was more or less accepted by the <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> (truly, sergeant Barrack tried to shout something about the necessity to maintain constant training and not just from time to time). <clr>Gaals, Humans<clrEnd> and <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd> were also in general pleased. But the <clr>Faes<clrEnd> were grunting that it's much better to read some scientific book or talk with your colleagues about work at least, instead of visiting the gym.
jump.232.text: And why should I support it?
jump.232.desc:
- Right! - someone of the <clr>Faes<clrEnd> exclaimed. - The brain is the main thing, anything else will come!

- Not the brains but the money, - one of the <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd> objected, - but everything else is right. 

- Now I will kick someone! - enraged sergeant Barrack shouted, rolling up his sleeves. The watch-out security guards rushed to quench the fire before it spread so that the press conference could be continued without victims.
jump.233.text: I regularly took to yoga and meditation
jump.233.desc: <clr>Gaals and Humans<clrEnd> started to respect you right away, for their meditation, yoga, occult and other shuck schools have long been arguing whose school is more ancient and who stole whose method of penetrating into the essence of the being. But the <clr>Maloqs, Faes and Pelengs<clrEnd> could not restrain themselves from showing contempt to such an idiotic method of doing one's physical exercises and were showing quite emphatically what they think about you.
jump.234.text: Real ranger must first of all keep his banking account in fitness and not his physical shape!
jump.234.desc: <clr>Humans and Pelengs<clrEnd> showed their complete solidarity with you - one's banking account is no doubt much more important than one's health! But the <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> were very close to kicking your face having found that this sounded almost like an insult on the their race. The real warrior doesn't care about banking account. <clr>Faes and Gaals<clrEnd> were in general indifferent towards such a response.
jump.235.text: I smoke hash and think I am a tough body-builder
jump.235.desc: Your reply provoked vivid applause among the <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd>, and the <clr>Humans<clrEnd> seemed also to be not completely void of humour. But all the rest decided that you're just mocking them, and the <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> were offended the most.
jump.236.text: Go to the electoral committee and see how the vote count is done
jump.237.text: Same thing as now - the money!
jump.237.desc: Derided in his best feelings, Blub Lubb has taken his seat. His irritation spread throughout all the <clr>Faeyan<clrEnd> and a part of <clr>Gaalian <clrEnd> seats. The <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> were displeased without anyone's help  - real warrior despises money! But the <clr>Humans<clrEnd> known across the Galaxy as the admirers of hard currency and also the <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd> - will now treat you with much more warmth.
jump.238.text: It's not good to bribe, everything must be done strictly according to the law!
jump.238.desc: Applause of the <clr>Gaalian<clrEnd> journalists was equal in its loudness to the jeering and laughter heard from the <clr>Peleng and Human <clrEnd> sectors. But the <clr>Faes and the Maloqs<clrEnd>, seemed to be also pleased with your reply, for they both think that the laws are made to be abided by.
jump.239.text: Most of all I loved the baseball bat - you can play baseball with it or kick someone if the need occurs!
jump.239.desc: Baseball is a Human game, so that the sympathies of <clr>Humans<clrEnd> were all yours. Alternative use of the bat was acclaimed by the <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> and <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd>. But the <clr>Gaals<clrEnd> and <clr>Faeyns<clrEnd> were offended - first by your open aggressiveness, and second by boldface digressing from the question asked by Blub Lubb.
jump.240.text: And where did you get it that I went to school at all?!
jump.240.desc: No one could understand what you were counting for in providing an answer like that. Ignoramuses can now provoke sympathy only among <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd>, and the <clr>Faes<clrEnd> treat you now as a duffer...
jump.241.text: I liked all the subjects, I was always keen on learning!
jump.241.desc: This was just the kind of answer the Faeyan teacher was hoping to get as well as the whole <clr>Faeyan<clrEnd> sector. The <clr>Gaals<clrEnd> also liked your quest for knowledge. But the <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd> and <clr>Humans<clrEnd> treated your words with suspect - if you're so smart, why are you a ranger still, and not in a big business or pirating? The <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> just screw up their faces showing you contempt, for the Regulations say: "You can never get smarter than your commander no matter how hard you try!"
jump.242.text: Most of all I liked the military science. Can't you see that from me?!
jump.242.desc: - Yeah, right! - Blub Lubb remarked sarcastically, sitting down. But the ironic comments of the <clr>Faes<clrEnd> and the <clr>Gaals<clrEnd> were overwhelmed by a roar of admiration on the part of the <clr>Maloq<clrEnd> journalists. The  <clr>Humans<clrEnd> and <clr>Pelengs<clrEnd> also received your reply rather benevolently.
jump.243.text: I enjoyed the Humanities, like Ethics or Philosophy
jump.243.desc: If you were intended to gain the respect of the <clr>Gaals<clrEnd>, you have hit it right! The <clr>Humans<clrEnd> also liked subjects of this kind, but the <clr>Pelengs, Faes<clrEnd> and especially <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd> had completely opposite opinions.
jump.244.text: I loved the sciences, they can be applied somehow at least, unlike the Humanities nonsense!
jump.244.desc: Your response provokes an ambiguous reaction. On the one hand, the sciences enjoy great respect of the <clr>Faeyan, Pelengs<clrEnd> and even <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd>! But the <clr>Humans<clrEnd> and especially <clr>Gaals<clrEnd> were not at all pleased with your attack.

jump.251.text: You can buy good gun for this money, after which there should be no more problems concerning the permits
jump.251.desc:
- Yeah, this is how the real <clr>Maloq<clrEnd> would answer! - shouted one of the members of that militaristic race.

- Nothing will be gained by such methods!!! - the <clr>Gaals and Faes<clrEnd> exclaimed in unison.

- Yeah, it may not work! - Hush Baba agreed. - Especially concerning the Mafioso... But the idea is interesting!

- A gun will always find use, - proclaimed someone from the <clr>Humans<clrEnd>. - This is a good investment.
jump.252.text: You should pay the Mafioso and he will deal with the others on his own part
jump.252.desc:
- Yes, this is the best decision! - Shooch Yaa exclaimed. - Where have you got this knowledge of life?? You must be are a regular viewer of my program "The Law and How to Get around It"...

The <clr>Humans<clrEnd> seemed to share the <clr>Peleng<clrEnd> standpoint completely, but all the other races' attitude was not so friendly.

- Are you not ashamed to pay the Mafiosi?! - A <clr>Gaal<clrEnd> expressed everyone's opinion. - This money will surely be directed for the development of Pirating, drug trafficking and other shady business!!! Shame...
jump.253.text: I think it's better to start your own business in a different location!
jump.253.desc: Your joke was a good thing to dissipate the tension. Everyone, except the <clr>Maloqs<clrEnd>, who found some non-patriotic lining in it, seemed to like it.
jump.254.text: You should set the Mayor against various committees and then inform on the local Mafiosi chief to the police, after which you can quickly gather all the required signatures when everyone will be fighting
jump.254.desc:
- Yeah! - Hush Baba said. - If you will remain alive after informing on the Mafiosi chief!

- All right, - a <clr>Gaal<clrEnd> suddenly spoke up for you. - Let's not gratify corrupted officials!

- And the main thing is that you will save money! - A <clr>Human<clrEnd> journalist said with a smile of satisfaction. - Perfect decision!

And only the <clr>Maloiqs and Faes<clrEnd>, who were very far from any problems of power were not reacting at all.
jump.255.text: You should pay the Mayor and the Police Chief, and then win the rest with their help
jump.255.desc:
- This can work, - Hush Baba murmured deep in thought. - The only thing is that 1000 cr will hardly be enough to satisfy their appetites...

The others reacted rather sluggishly. All were in general abusing the local prostitute functionaries...
jump.256.text: You should save as much money as you can so that there'll be enough to bribe everyone.
jump.256.desc:
Your naïve response provoked everyone's laughter in the sector of the <clr>Humans, Maloqs and Pelengs<clrEnd>.

- You will not save so much money in all your life! - they shouted. - The money will never be enough to bribe everyone!

<clr>The gaals<clrEnd> were outraged with your response:

- This is why we have corruption! - they claimed. - You should not tolerate bribers!!!

And only the <clr>Faes<clrEnd>, who not at all engaged in business or small politics, found you verdict to be judicious and logical.
